title.en: The setup wizard stops offering itself once an agent exists

description.en: The Marketplace decided this from an agent list that could come back empty while the core was still loading — read as "this machine has no agents", with nothing polling to correct it, so the button stayed for an agent that had been set up minutes earlier. A detail page now keeps the list it already has when the request fails, brings the core up instead of answering empty, and refreshes the moment the wizard creates an agent.

title.en: Model lists and connection tests survive a slow first request

description.en: Both gave up after 15 seconds and never tried again, so a relay that was merely cold came back as a broken key — and went through when the user pressed the same button a second time. A connection test, which is a real request to the model, now waits up to 45 seconds; a model listing waits 20. Either retries once when nothing answered at all. What the endpoint itself rejects, such as an invalid key, is still reported straight away.

title.en: The account sign-in tab no longer shows the API form's model

description.en: Uninstalling without deleting data keeps the saved key and model, as intended. That model then also appeared under Account sign-in, naming something the signed-in account may never have served. The sign-in tab now starts empty whenever an API key is on file — and the model chosen there is saved, where previously it was discarded.

title.en: Agents install and update from one channel

description.en: The per-agent Stable / Beta / Nightly selector is gone. It never affected what the page reported as the newest version — that always came from the stable release — so switching it produced no visible change, and the pre-release names it assumed only exist for two of the agents on offer: elsewhere the same button either failed outright or fetched a build older than the one already installed. Installs and updates now come from each agent's current release.

title.en: A paired device is a finished setup

description.en: The panel's button is now the large primary action and names its destination — back to the browser to add an agent — while the footer keeps its own route into the local agent steps. Both end with an agent in the paired workspace; what separates them is where you do the work, and the step's copy now says so instead of claiming everything happens in the workspace from then on. The step tracker also stops promising the three optional steps to someone who is about to press "Finish setup": pairing completes setup, so the rail and the dots show that path until the user asks for the local continuation.
